Galway County Council representatives met with the Chair and the Board of the Irish 
Cultural Centre (ICC) Boston to strengthen collaboration and acknowledge the Centre’s 
ongoing development of its 61-acre cultural, sporting, educational, and business campus.

the importance of connecting the Irish diaspora with these businesses. They offered strong 
support for Galway LEO companies seeking 
to expand into the United States. 
The Centre outlined its plans to further 
enhance its facilities and programmes and 
expressed sincere appreciation for Galway 
County Council’s visit and recognition of 
their work.

IRISH OFFICE 
Seachtain na Gaeilge takes place annually from 1–17 March, and this year Galway County 
Council played a leading role in promoting Irish-language events across the county. Activities 
were hosted in Áras an Chontae, local libraries, and schools, ensuring that communities 
throughout Galway could take part in the celebration of Irish culture and heritage. 
The Council’s Seachtain na Gaeilge programme was officially launched on Monday, 23 
February. The event opened with vibrant and uplifting performances by Carmel Dempsey, 
Brenda Curtin, and Frankie Colohan, setting an energetic tone for the festivities ahead. 
Following the music, attendees were given an overview of the wide range of events 
scheduled to take place across the county during Seachtain na Gaeilge.

range of handmade products. Each crafter engaged with visitors using at least basic Irish

HEALTHY IRELAND 
 
THE WOMEN’S HEALTH PROGRAMME 
The Empowering Women’s Health programme is now underway, 
with a series of free, live-streamed workshops taking place 
throughout March and broadcast to community locations across 
County Galway, including the offshore islands. This initiative will 
bring expert talks live streamed directly into local hubs, ensuring 
that women can access high quality, 
evidence- based- information on 
perimenopause, menopause, and post 
menopause. Each weekly session 
includes both expert talks and practical 
demonstrations, creating an accessible, supportive, learning 
environment for women attending.

18 
 
The three-week series will cover a broad range of topics, including sleep and healthy ageing, 
nutrition, pelvic health, exercise therapy, breathwork, resistance training, and general 
women’s health. By working with a team of community facilitators around the county, the 
programme will provide women with actionable guidance to 
support their physical and mental wellbeing at this important life 
stage.  
This initiative has been developed in partnership with Healthy 
Ireland, the HSE, Forum Connemara, Comhair na nOileain, GSP 
and Family Resource Centres, across the county. The strong 
collaborative approach ensures that the programme is both 
inclusive and accessible, strengthening community engagement 
while supporting women’s health.  
DEMENTIA CAFÉ INITAITVE 
The Memory Café initiative continues to strengthen community-based support for people 
living with dementia and their careers across 
Connemara. Monthly cafés currently operate in 
Clifden, Oughterard, Roundstone and Letterfrack, 
offering informal, welcoming spaces that reduce 
isolation and encourage meaningful social 
connection. Attendance remains consistently 
strong, demonstrating sustained community need 
and positive engagement. 
A diverse programme of activities has been 
scheduled for 2026, offering a balance of creative, physical, sensory, and wellbeing focused 
sessions tailored to the needs of participants. Activities include arts and crafts projects such 
as making St. Brigid’s crosses, felt craft workshops, Jenga and aquapainting, Easter bonnet 
decorating, bird feeder and birdbox painting, reminiscence teas, musical memories, Irish 
music and dance, gardening, and Qigong chair exercises. Additional specialist inputs include 
talks from community physiotherapists on the importance of movement, HSE talks on 5 
Ways to Wellbeing, chiropody information sessions, and music and song delivered by local 
musicians. This varied schedule ensures that cafés remain engaging throughout the year 
while supporting cognitive stimulation, dexterity, mood, and social participation.  
A 2025 investment was also made by Healthy County Galway in dementia specific activity 
packs such as Aqua paint sets, puzzles, musical bingo, sensory items, reminiscence 
materials, and aromatherapy kits, ensuring that each café is equipped with creative and 
stimulating resources.  
COMMUNITY SUPPORT CENTRES – RECENT DEVELOPMENTS 
Significant progress has been made in strengthening the Community Support Centre (CSC) 
network to improve local resilience during severe weather and emergency events.

19 
 
Expressions of Interest have been sought from community facilities interested in acting as 
CSCs, with a strong response received. This process is supporting the development of a 
more structured and geographically balanced network across the county, aligned with 
vulnerability and coverage considerations. Premises eligible to be CSCs have been listed on 
the Council website and categorised by Municipal District, adding accessibility information 
and incorporating new centres on an ongoing basis. https://www.galway.ie/en/community-
tourism-arts/community-development/community-support-centres. 
An updated CSC operating procedure has been issued and reviewed by the Major 
Emergency Development Committee and the Local Coordination Group, clarifying roles, 
activation protocols, generator access arrangements and funding parameters, in line with 
national guidance. The CSC points of contact and elected members are to be invited on 
Thursday 26th March to an information session on the operating procedures.  
 
In accordance with Circular EM 12/2025 on the installation of changeover switches for 
mobile generators, three Community Support Centres were designated for funded rewiring 
works to facilitate generator deployment. The centres identified were Clifden Town Hall, 
Seanscoil Shailearna, and Dunmore Town Hall. These facilities were selected based on 
geographic spread, suitability and their role within the emerging CSC network. The 
designated centres were contacted and requested to submit quotations for the necessary 
electrical works. Works, focused specifically on enabling safe connection of mobile 
generators via compliant changeover switches is underway.  
 
Community facilities not included in the current funded rewiring allocation were advised of 
the availability of the Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) as a potential source of support 
for essential infrastructure upgrades, including rewiring works to facilitate generator use.

CLÁR  2026 PROGRAMME  
The Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, Dara Calleary TD on 
10th March 2026 announced an expansion of the CLÁR programme.  For County Galway this 
involves inclusion of one additional Electoral Division, An Crompán in Connemara Municipal 
District and Gaeltacht which incorporates An Cheathrú Rua and surrounding areas for the 
first time under the CLÁR Programme.   
 
CLÁR (Ceantair Laga Árd-Riachtanais) is a targeted investment programme for rural areas 
that aims to provide funding for small infrastructural projects in designated rural areas that 
have experienced significant levels of de-population and/or socio-economic disadvantage 
and geographic remoteness. The funding assists in building the resilience of these rural 
communities and for 2026 it will continue to be rolled out over three Measures.  
 
MEASURE 1 COMMUNITY AMENITIES AND FACILITIES 
Applications are made directly to the Rural Team in Galway County Council who will be 
seeking Applications in the period March 31st to May 15th, 2026, via the SUBMIT Application 
Platform.  Webinars on CLÁR are proposed for Tuesday March 24th and Tuesday April 14th, 
2026, with promotion via County Galway PPN and in local media.   Interested Organisations 
can contact clar@galwaycoco.ie

CHANGES TO THE PROGRAMME FOR 2026  
Development of community facilities and amenities including sports facilities, youth clubs, 
teenage spaces, playgrounds, sensory gardens, walking tracks and much more.  There are 
new items eligible for support this year under Measure 1, including support for traffic safety 
measures with a particular link to community facilities or events, and for initiatives aimed at 
reducing light pollution in rural communities.  Funding for Emergency Generators can be 
considered.  
 
A ban is to take effect in 2031 that limits the materials used to refill Astro surfaces. For 
applicants considering submitting an application under the 2026 CLÁR programme for the 
development of, or works on, any type of Astro surface, they should in the first instance 
discuss these regulations with their contractor or surface supplier to ensure that their 
development is fully compliant with relevant legislation and is future proofed so as to 
ensure best value for money and longevity of the surface for users. The application form 
must clearly outline the need and rationale for the projects put forward. The local authority 
is advised to contact the Department in respect of any queries regarding project eligibility 
 
For Emergency Generators, these must be mobile to allow for shared community use. There 
must be confirmation that the facilities that will use the generator have changeover 
switches in place and the cost of installing these switches in these facilities can be included 
as part of the generator project application  
 
The following projects are ineligible under the CLÁR programme Footpaths • Bus shelters • 
Works to current school buildings which are not open to the public after school hours • 
CCTV • The purchase of land or buildings.   
 
In May 2026, there will be a further eight projects due for completion under the 2024 CLÁR 
Scheme and ten projects are also live under the CLÁR 2025 Scheme with a completion date 
of May 2027 but half of these due to progress to completion by the end of 2026.

TUAM MD DRINKING BYE-LAWS 
Public drinking in Tuam MD, particularly within parks and commercial areas, has been 
identified as an ongoing issue, giving rise to concerns in relation to public safety, amenity, 
and litter. While national legislation provides enforcement powers to An Garda Síochána, 
these powers are largely reactive and generally apply once behaviour has escalated, limiting 
opportunities for early intervention and prevention. In response, it is proposed to review 
and progress the Municipal District of Tuam (Control of Consumption and Possession of 
Alcohol in Public Places) Bye-law. The draft bye-law would prohibit the consumption of 
alcohol, or possession with intent to consume, in designated public places. Enforcement 
measures would include the use of fixed‑payment notices and powers for An Garda 
Síochána and authorised persons to direct individuals to desist and to confiscate alcohol 
where appropriate. Exemptions would apply in respect of major events and licensed 
outdoor seating areas. 
 
The draft Drinking Bye-law was presented to the Tuam MD Members on Monday 9 March at 
the Tuam MD Municipal District Meeting. The draft bye‑laws will be available for public 
inspection during a four‑week consultation period from Wednesday, 18 March 2026, to 
Friday, 17 April 2026 in the Tuam Municipal District office and the Tuam Library.  The Public 
Notice will be published in local newspapers on the 18 March, stating the intention to make 
a Bye-law. Members of the public may make submissions or observations in writing or by 
email to communitysafety@galwaycoco.ie which will end on the 24 April. The bye-Law will 
be presented to the Tuam MD on the 8 June, including any submissions received, for 
adoption and may be adopted with or without consultation related amendments. Expected 
commencement of the bye-law is Tuesday 7 July.

buildings, with top‑ups of €20,000–€40,000 depending on the number of residential

• A new grant targeted at bringing vacant floors above commercial premises back into 
residential use. 
• Funding of up to €95,000 for a single unit, with additional top‑ups for multi‑unit 
conversions  
• Recognises added costs such as fire separation and independent access.

• A grant of up to €5,000 (or 67% of report cost) to support feasibility and technical

projects.  
• Available where two or more residential units are proposed or for over‑the‑shop 
conversions. 
• Reports must be prepared by a registered architect, engineer, or surveyor acting as 
an assigned certifier. 
4. VPRG FOR WHOLE‑BUILDING COMMERCIAL CONVERSIONS 
• Enhanced top‑ups on the standard €50,000/€70,000 grant where two or more 
residential units are being created from a full commercial building conversions.  
• Maximum top‑up of €40,000 per building. 
• A single grant applies per building, with a charge placed on the entire building and 
clawback linked to number of units and timeframes. 
5. ADMINISTRATIVE AND DELIVERY IMPLICATIONS FOR LOCAL AUTHORITIES 
These enhancements are expected to: 
• Increase the volume and complexity of VPRG applications.

LOCAL IMPROVEMENT SCHEME (LIS) 
Galway County Council welcomes the national increase in Local Improvement Scheme (LIS) 
funding to €17.55 million for 2026, as well as the early launch of the programme which 
supports more timely delivery of works this year. 
 
Galway County Council received €1,170,380 for 2026 and a further €250,00 was ringfenced 
for the islands, a total of €1,420,380.  
 
Galway County Council previously had a calling for LIS applications in 2024, and we also 
continue to hold applications carried forward from the previous round. In total, the Council 
currently has 225 applications on hand. 
 
The Department of Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht has set a return 
deadline of close of business on 25th March 2026 for a priority list which is currently being 
created for consideration under the 2026 allocation. 
 
Recently, we are seeing an increase in the number of applications with estimated costs in 
the region of €200,000–€300,000. To put this in context, a single project of this scale can be 
equivalent to the full annual LIS allocation for an entire Municipal District. As a result, even 
where funding is increased nationally, the delivery capacity per MD is effectively 
constrained by the number of large‑scale applications currently in the system. These higher-
cost schemes, while often fully justified due to road length or condition, have a significant 
impact on overall programme throughput. The presence of several such applications within 
the same MD may limit the number of schemes that can be advanced in any given year and 
will contribute to longer waiting periods for applicants, especially where large projects rank 
highly in the priority list. 
 
Due to the high volume of applications relative to the available national allocation, it is 
important to highlight that many applicants will still face significant waiting periods before 
their road can be considered for funding. This is consistent with previous years of the 
scheme, where demand has exceeded the annual budget. Galway County Council will 
continue to assess all applications in line with national guidelines, prioritise schemes fairly 
and transparently based on the agreed criteria, and keep applicants and Councillors 
informed on progress as the 2026 process advances.

HOP TO IT COMMON FROG SURVEY – COUNTY GALWAY (2026) 
The Biodiversity Office issued a public press release in March 2026 to support the Irish 
Peatland Conservation Council (IPCC) Hop To It Frog Survey and encourage public 
participation across County Galway. The campaign seeks to address a significant data gap, as 
only five frog records were submitted from County Galway in 2025, limiting understanding 
of the local status of the Common Frog. 
The press release highlights the importance of citizen science in building robust biodiversity 
datasets and positions the Common Frog (Rana temporaria) as a key biological indicator of 
environmental health. The species is Ireland’s only native frog and is legally protected under 
the EU Habitats Directive and the Wildlife Acts, as well as being listed as Vulnerable at a 
European level. 
Galway County Council is supporting the IPCC in promoting the 2026 Hop To It Frog Survey, 
which records sightings of frogspawn, tadpoles, froglets and adult frogs. Members of the 
public are encouraged to submit records directly to the IPCC or via the National Biodiversity 
Data Centre, strengthening both local and national biodiversity monitoring.

evidence‑based decision‑making, supports 
national conservation efforts, and aligns with 
the Council’s role under the Ceangal 
Programme in raising public awareness and
